newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures sharply up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures sharply up on short-covering.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo corn futures ended sharply higher across the board on Wednesday, lifted by short-covering and supported by the yen's weaker tone against the dollar and a firmer Chicago market overnight, traders said. Prices ranged from 300 yen to 780 yen per tonne higher. Benchmark September was up 300 yen to 15,300 yen. Daily volume was 46,857 lots.

Prices extended early gains as active short-covering in nearby months spilled over into other contracts. But private investors remained cautious about fresh buying ahead of a U.S. Department of Agriculture report due out later this week.
The spot December contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.96 per bushel at 0745 GMT, down by 0-1/2 U.S. cent from Tuesday's close.
The spot November CBOT soybean futures contract was at $7.32 at 0741 GMT, up by 0-1/2 cent from Tuesday's close.
